answer.read: Blankstahl opened at its first quote of six-ten, no clause, thirty days, twelve months, and justified it with year-on-year index rises [S]. Two things work against it. The alloy surcharge fell over the last quarter (a1 [D]), and its own should-cost estimate sits well below the quote [E]. It strongly wants volume and binding commitment, because small accounts are under review [Z volume, planning_security]. It also wants protection on AS-14404 [Z material_risk]. Squeezing too hard risks it deprioritising us [Z deprioritising_us], and we depend on it for 370011 [Z single_source].
answer.message: Thank you for your offer. We see a long-term partnership in this part and are prepared to commit to a thirty-six month term with the forecast volume, which gives you the planning security and volume basis you value. Given the recent decline in the alloy surcharge and our established price history, we propose the terms on the attached sheet. We'd value your feedback and are open to discussing how we structure this together fairly.
answer.reason: O6 gives nearly the lowest C of all the options. It offers the longest commitment, which the supplier values most [Z] but which the 'to it' figure does not count, so it should be received better than the -20% suggests. O5 has the same C on twenty-four months but gives the supplier less. E0 and O2 match O6 on the thirty-six month term but come out at a higher C. The clause options cost us more C and give away an index protection we can trade later.
